To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an ovine intra follicular peptide regulates oocyte maturation and antral but not preantral growth and cumulus expansion in buffalo.

the ovine follicular peptide isolated in the present investigation inhibits oocyte maturation and antral, but not preantral, follicle growth and also affects the protein, calcium, phosphorus contents of the oocytes.
the isolated ovine follicle fluid peptide has a negative impact on buffalo oocyte maturation and antral but not preantral growth in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of an intraovarian factor that may regulate folliculogenesis and oocyte maturation in buffalo.

a novel approach to identify and characterize the intrafollicular peptides that regulate oocyte and follicle development in the buffalo, a species with limited availability of in vitro models for oocyte and follicular development.
the identification of an intrafollicular peptide(s) that regulates folliculogenesis and oocyte maturation in a heterologuous species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peptide fraction isolated from ovine FF has a potential role in oocyte and antraI follicle maturation, but not in somatic cell proliferation and monolayer formation.
the isolated peptide from ovine follicles is a potential intrafollicular regulator of oocyte maturation and antral growth in buffalo.
the isolated peptide is not an oocyte maturation inhibitor but an intrafollicular growth factor that regulates oocyte and an antral follicular development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a peptide from ovine follicles is capable of regulating the development of oocytes and antral (but not preantral) follicles in buffalo.

the peptide isolated from the follicular fluid of sheep has a negative effect on oocyte maturation and antral but not preantral buffalo follicle development in vitro and has no effect on the growth and differentiation of somatic cells in buffalo.

ovine follicular peptide(s) isolated and purified from ovine follicles can be used to regulate the growth of oocyte, antral follicular, cumulus, granulosa, and oviducal epithelial cells in vitro in buffalo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intraovarian peptides may have species specificity and that they may have different functions in different mammalian species.
the intrafollicular peptides play an important role in regulating oocyte maturation and antral growth of buffalo oocytes and follicles.
intrafollicular factors are not only species specific but also follicle size dependent.
